fields.label: the Cracked Lands
fields.description: Dry, cracked, shadowed canyon country under a hard sun — most of the time. Rarely and without warning, the water comes down: a wall tearing through the canyon floor that drowns whatever stands in it and leaves real soil behind once it drains. Warning chimes ring ahead of the flood for anyone who knows to listen.

fields.label: nabbuq
fields.description: Fist-sized indigo-violet bladders crowded under lavender bracts, half sunk in the cool soil of the shade line. They swell after a flood and keep their water for weeks. Cut, they are a sweet, filling vegetable.

fields.label: ruqqal
fields.description: Dense tufts of twisted coral-salmon stalks, wrung like wet rope and striped with dried flood mud. The stalks cure in the channel silt; cut and combed they spin into a coarse, warm cloth.

fields.label: sevvuq
fields.description: Skull-sized, brain-folded globes in saffron going to sulfur, studded along the flood high-water line like a row of lamps. The folds weep a yellow pigment that stains whatever it touches.

fields.label: zennaq
fields.description: A waist-high burst of stiff wire-thin filaments splayed like a frayed broom, verdigris-copper at the base and silver at the tips. It is dry as tinder, and in a storm it stands up to the sky: lightning on the mesa tops prefers it to the ground.

fields.label: luqqim
fields.description: Clusters of translucent tulip cups, magenta shading to amethyst with a cyan rim, growing only in the deepest slot-canyon dark. Each cup holds a faint cold glow, enough to find the way by and not enough to read.

fields.label: harrovaq
fields.description: The canyon's own tree: a low, wide, twisted trunk of slate-blue bark leaning hard toward the wall, bone-white corkscrew branches without a leaf, and burgundy tassels that hang in place of fruit. It roots in the floor soil beside the cliff, never in the rock.

fields.label: twisting thornwood
fields.description: A large species of tree found in polluted arid environments. It is one of three closely related species of plant, alongside the thornweed and thorngrass.

fields.label: twisting thorngrass
fields.description: Similar to grass yet covered in small thorn-like structures. It is related in part to the twisting thornwood and thornweed.

fields.label: twisting thornweed
fields.description: A bush-sized plant related to the thornwood tree, hardy enough to survive on heavily polluted ground.

fields.label: veqma
fields.description: A wiry, near-leafless plant of the shade line — mostly taproot, the visible growth a sparse fan of tough grey-green whip-stems rising from one deep crown. Its root finds the hidden water, and its stem tips blush green in proportion to how near the water table sits: dull grey where it lies deep, brightening cell by cell toward the seep, vivid over a find. A stand of veqma is a contour map. Reading one is the first thing a Farmer teaches a child.

fields.label: flood-born
fields.description: Hatched from eggs that waited years in the dry clay, in the hours after the flood receded. A flood-born irqit lives only as long as the mud stays wet: it breeds once, lays into the clay, and dies where it stands as the ground stiffens.

fields.label: irqit
fields.description: Palm-sized and soft-bodied, glossy wet skin over a quick paddling scramble — the irqit exists as eggs in the dry clay for years, waiting. When the flood recedes, every soaked cell turns into a nursery: a sudden carpet of small frantic life between the roar and the dry. Each one breeds exactly once, lays into the wet clay, and dies as the mud stiffens. It is a living calendar of the flood, gone as completely as it arrived.

fields.label: tarruq
fields.description: A lean, long-limbed climber built for the vertical dark of the crack network — grip-padded feet, a deep resonating throat-chamber that carries its low territorial calls for hundreds of meters, each animal answering its neighbors down the line. On an ordinary day the Cracked Lands' soundscape is wind, then tarruq, then wind. It goes silent and climbs when the cracks begin to fill — a Farmer trusts that hush as the biome's second warning, before even the chimes.

fields.label: wound-stone
fields.description: Near-instant clotting that ossifies into dense, stone-like formations wherever an uttaqar is wounded — the same process the crag giants use in place of scars. Provides ablative protection and slows blood loss while it lasts; old uttaqar carry layers of it like tree rings.

fields.label: rock troll
fields.description: A colossal, eyeless creature that owns the Cracked Lands' crag walls, talus slopes and slot-canyon dark the way the muttavaq owns the flats — it surfaces from its lair only when provoked. Lacking real regeneration, it answers every wound with stone: ultra-fast clotting ossifies into dense ablative formations within minutes, so an old uttaqar reads as more rock than flesh, seamed with wound-stone in layers a Farmer can count like tree rings.

fields.label: muttavaq
fields.description: A canyon-floor giant that sleeps for years under a clay pan the eye reads as ordinary terrain — a low mounded polygon field a touch too regular, cracks radiating from a center dried clay never makes on its own. Walk the famous cracked-pan flats and you walk on sleeping animals; walk THIS pan and you walk on one animal. It never hunts, never raids and never manhunters, awake or asleep — the flood wakes it wherever the water reaches, and it spends the flood-weeks wading the wet floor as a walking weir, straining mud and carrion through its jaw-plates. At the dry it digs in wherever it stands and becomes terrain again, somewhere new. Its burrow-lining is the planet's largest single crack-wax deposit; killing one asleep is easy, shameful, and a fortune.

fields.label: nabbuq bladder
fields.description: A water-heavy indigo bladder, sweet and crisp. Eaten raw it is a perfectly good vegetable.

fields.label: ruqqal cloth
fields.description: A coarse coral-coloured cloth spun from ruqqal stalks. Rough on the skin and warm for its weight.

fields.label: zennaq filament
fields.description: A bundle of springy verdigris-copper wires pulled from a zennaq. They conduct well enough to bind a coil and are brittle enough to snap at the second bend.

fields.label: fossil impression
fields.description: A hand-sized slab of canyon-wall stone, split to show the pressed print of something that lived and died here in a wetter age — a fern-mat, a shell-bed, a trackway crossing the face. Common enough that every wall near the water line has a few, and worth a modest sum to anyone off-world who has never seen a sky this dry.

fields.label: articulated fossil skeleton
fields.description: A whole small animal, curled in death and caught whole in the stone — every joint still in place after however many thousand floods. Rare enough that a Farmer who finds one tells the story for years, and serious money to anyone building a collection.

fields.label: deep-stratum fossil
fields.description: A heavy dark slab from the oldest layers the canyon walls expose — strata so old they read almost black, holding the edge of something immense: massive plated bone, mineral-dark, still curled the way it fell asleep. Whatever it is, it was already ancient when the flood started cutting this ground. Quest-grade; museum-grade; the kind of find a Farmer keeps quiet about until they've decided who deserves to know.

fields.label: flood-buried hull
fields.description: A hull section half buried in dried flood mud, uncovered by the last flood. Deconstruct it before the next one takes it back.

fields.label: flood-buried speeder
fields.description: The shell of a small repulsor craft, nose down in the mud where a flood rolled it. Deconstruct it for valuable resources.

fields.label: fossil display slab
fields.description: A dressed stone frame bolted flat to the wall, holding a fossil slab presented like a museum plaque. Every Cracked Lands homestead has at least one; a gravship galley with one bolted to the bulkhead is saying the crew has been somewhere worth remembering.

fields.label: fossil skeleton mount
fields.description: A worked stone-and-metal armature holding a complete articulated skeleton upright in display pose. The centerpiece of the room it stands in — Farmers who find a whole animal in the wall build one of these instead of selling the find.

fields.label: fossil-bearing wall (impressions)
fields.description: A stretch of canyon wall where the strata run pale and close-banded — split it and the odds favor a fern-mat, a shell-bed, a trackway. The common find, but the walls hold thousands of them.

fields.label: fossil-bearing wall (articulated)
fields.description: A denser run of strata, the kind that sometimes holds a whole animal instead of a print. Rarer along the wall line — and worth the extra work to dig out clean.

fields.label: fossil-bearing wall (deep stratum)
fields.description: Strata so old they read almost black, found only deep in the walls or where a flood has just cut a fresh face. What is in here is old enough that nobody is sure what it is until it is out.

fields.endMessage: The floodwater is draining into the cracks. The canyon floor is soil now, where it wasn't before.
fields.letterText: The chimes were right — the wall has arrived. Water is tearing through the canyon floor.
fields.label: canyon flood
fields.description: The wall has arrived. Red-brown water is tearing through the canyon floor, drowning anything caught below the ledges. It will recede on its own, leaving real soil where the dry cracked clay was.

fields.label: crack-wax suit
fields.description:
A full-body suit of stiffened fabric over a rigid frame, sealed watertight under a coat of smoothed crack-wax — the same waterproofing the Sealed shed from their burrows and the Farmers line their cisterns with, now worn. Heavy, slow and hot, but it keeps a pawn dry and breathing while they cross or work the Cracked Lands' flooded ground.

Terrain only. This suit does not let anyone dive to a sea floor or come back from one — nothing does, except a ship.

fields.label: peakstorm light
fields.description: Clear and dry overhead, while the far skyline flickers and grumbles with a storm on the peaks upstream. Nothing falls here. The water it is making will arrive later, down the canyons.
